title: Moonshot waves at blocks 2 and 3: the everything-free game and mixed units
made_with: AI agents (Claude) directed by the author
lean: nothing in this section is checked in Lean; no person has read its proofs

findings.statement: Theorem 2W: at block 2, W arrays need at least 2W paid moves in every game whose free steps touch a bounded number of entries per row (engine, widened and everything-free games), so block 2 never saves; with the two-layer bound, every unit with W >= 2 arrays at block m needs at least max(W + m, 2W) moves.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic re-derived it line by line and found no error, and checked its key orthogonality fact with its own code over a wider menu of free steps; the wave note recommends a second skeptic; no person has read it
supersedes: 2-adic parity lattice bound 5W/3 for division-free units at block 2 (mw-xw2tight)
open-directions-3 section 8: plain chain map with running-XOR inverse open at block 2

findings.statement: Theorem 2W': W targets that each apply at least two directions need at least 2W single-direction paid moves; rank-2 targets never save, and a mixed unit needs at least 2(W_K + W_R) moves.
findings.status_detail: same proof and same skeptic as Theorem 2W; the skeptic checked that it applies to the mixed tracks' two-row targets and checked the exclusion arithmetic

excluded: rank-2 7 in 13 and 9 in 17 at block 3

findings.statement: Two-layer bound (Theorem T'): every unit with W >= 2 arrays at block m needs at least W + m paid moves, in every game with bounded free steps; in the everything-free game it excludes the exact 2 in 3 at block 2 (0.415), with or without division by 2, and 2 in 4 and 3 in 5 at block 3; at block 5 it excludes 2 in 6 (0.317).
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic upheld the trace-limit version and reproduced its numbers (Lemma O overlaps, floors to f = 8) with its own code; the first version (engine and widened games only) never had a skeptic of its own

findings.statement: In the everything-free game, every-f identities can mix layers: conjugating the parity-phase identity P = (1+i)/2 + (1-i)/2 Z by D2 CS D1 equates a combination of one-move words with a free word (72 cases with four paid letters, none with three); so the engine-game proof of the two-layer bound does not transfer directly.
findings.status_detail: one program, the relation finder found 24 relations, all within one layer, in menus of 437 distinct words; not repeated by a skeptic

findings.statement: Corollary S: a unit for W arrays needs at least W deep moves (at the end of a chain of m moves) and W co-deep moves that read inputs; the shared-top families searched earlier in the everything-free game had one deep move for two arrays and could not contain a unit.
findings.status_detail: the first half of the two-layer proof that one skeptic upheld

findings.statement: Parity lattice: every free step of the everything-free game keeps the lattice of vectors whose entries agree modulo 1 - i and sum to an even number; at f = 2 a move pushes out 6 units and an array needs 10, so a unit that never divides by 2 needs at least 5/3 moves per array at block 2.
findings.status_detail: no skeptic read it; its two key numbers were computed four independent ways; superseded at block 2 by Theorem 2W for every unit

findings.statement: Reed-Muller lattices in the chi game at block 3 (Clifford steps plus the running XOR) give 2.327 moves per array at f = 3 and values rising toward 2.5 at larger odd f, which would exclude a 3 in 7 that never divides by 2 there.
findings.status_detail: the deciding value at f = 5 comes from a formula fitted to 161 exact values and has not been checked exactly; the exact f = 3 value misses by 0.006; no skeptic

findings.statement: Block 3, everything-free game: about 136 exact cross-talk tests (menus of 9 to 115 free words, 1 to 4 paid moves, shared first, middle and last moves and two shared moves in a row) found only trivial collapses (a direction applied twice); the skeptic's complete-span re-run flagged 34 collapses at f = 3, 4, and all were small-f coincidences (25, missing by 0.54 to 0.76 at f = 5) or trivial identities in disguise (9).
findings.status_detail: linear algebra in floating point (called exact in the notes with singular-value gaps of 10 to 14 orders); one skeptic re-ran it with the left-out terms and classified every flag; a second skeptic confirmed the parts it finished (three configurations and the identities at f = 3 to 7)

findings.statement: Within the menus tested, a shared move can serve two arrays at block 3 in the everything-free game only through a singular readout whose cancelling mix uses unboundedly long free words; such words exist (A.B has order 3, 7, 7, 31, 63 at f = 2..6).
findings.status_detail: the argument is the author's; the skeptic found its logic sound and corrected 'exponential order' to 'unbounded, erratic order'

findings.statement: Least squares over 574 (shape, direction pattern) pairs at block 3 in the everything-free game found no unit: best relative residual 0.427 (3 in 8) and 0.474 (2 in 5); a unit needs 0.
findings.status_detail: a numerical search found nothing; this is evidence, not proof; every shape first recovered a planted target

findings.statement: Theorem T: no exact unit that is exactly tight on the block-3 hook can give any array a two-row target, in the engine or widened game; excludes 1+4 in 10, 7+38 in 88, 2+8 in 20, 3+7 in 21, 4+21 in 49 and 10+35 in 91.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic re-derived it line by line; its finite input (no single first step into a two-row array passes: 0 of 14 engine classes, 0 of 1,680 widened classes, smallest miss sqrt 8) is checked by computer and was rebuilt by the skeptic in three arithmetics

findings.statement: Theorem S8 as written (separating packed two-row arrays costs at least 8 per array, in a two-level model with Levi letters) is wrong: the Levi group has 73,728 elements, not 8,192, its key 2 x 2 grid of kernels is 9 kernels, and the 'exhaustive' two-letter check covered only a subgroup.
findings.status_detail: refuted by its skeptic with its own code in two primes
findings.refuted_by: the skeptic's enumeration of the full Levi group (73,728 elements, 9 kernels)

findings.statement: In the strict two-level model with any finite group of Levi letters, separating packed two-row arrays costs at least 8 per array in the large-f limit; so that model excludes the block-3 mixed units with hook room 16.
findings.status_detail: the skeptic's own short repair (an information-set argument); no one has read it; every computed minimum was 8 per array

findings.statement: Symmetric programs split into a direct sum of smaller programs, one per symmetry type; with Theorem M's certificate this excludes engine 2+9 in 22, 10+35 in 91, 4+18 in 44 and 6+7 in 28 (exactly tight there, and no single first step into a kernel array passes); an order-4 twist leaves a loophole for two-row eigen-pieces.
findings.status_detail: no skeptic read it; the defect table it needs (6 or 7 on a kernel array) was later rebuilt over all 10,752 engine steps by another track and, from an independent model, by that track's skeptic; an analyst found the screen overcounts absorbed moves (no exclusion lost)

findings.statement: First-touch prices (Lemmas Q, Q1, Q2, Q3, Q''): the waste caused by the first move touching each array adds up and never exceeds the room; with exhaustive tables they force engine 1+5 in 12 into a narrow shape (kernel array's first touch at least 5 steps, each two-row array's at least 2, total waste at most 1) and every kernel array of engine 10+36 in 93 to be first touched by at least 3 steps.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic read every lemma line by line; the tables (Theorem M's 105 over all 10,752 engine steps; hook stable ranks over all 1,680 widened classes) are checked by computer and were rebuilt by the skeptic from an independent model

findings.statement: Conjecture FT, special case: touching one two-row array completely costs at least 8 when every touch draws its steps from an abelian group of Levi letters.
findings.status_detail: proved by the skeptic of the first-touch track (fractional subadditivity of rank over characters); no one has read it

findings.statement: At f = 2 every 12-move family for 1+5 in 12 stops at a quantised floor (0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or more); the best misses exactly the characters 001 and 101 of the kernel array, and the 1+1 in 4 relay that the hook forbids stops at the same 0.25, so 0.25 is not a near miss.
findings.status_detail: the f = 2 test is exact per program; the skeptic reproduced every saved floor with its own evaluator; that no 12-move program passes is evidence from the families tried, not proof

findings.statement: Approximate units: with bounded coefficients they obey the full bound W + m (Theorem B'); with exploding coefficients they can reach W + m - 1 at best, and a shape with t < W deep moves has large-f error at least W - t (Theorem B).
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic upheld it; the predicted floor 0.707 was measured at 0.699 and 0.711, and the skeptic reproduced it to f = 8

findings.statement: 'The one-move window W + m - 1 holds no useful approximate unit in the everything-free game' (wave 3).
findings.status_detail: refuted by its skeptic
findings.refuted_by: the relative exactification theorem needs no finite group; the running XOR on one bit row commutes exactly with the paid move on the other row (f = 1..8, unbounded order), and a toy family using that commutation has error exactly 0 at f = 2..5 under the relative recursion

findings.statement: At block 2 the recursion keeps exactly two kinds of identity whatever the smaller calls return: D1 D2 = D2 D1, and D1 commutes with every free step that touches only the other row; a full-value approximate 2 in 3 must blow up along a kept identity, and such identities (R8, R8') exist.
findings.status_detail: the identities are checked by computer at f = 1..5; one skeptic rebuilt them with its own code and read Lemmas H and K line by line

findings.statement: 'A unit without an exact twin must use the running XOR together with lamps, or D1 D2 = D2 D1' and 'families built on R8 are exact programs in disguise' (wave 4).
findings.status_detail: refuted by its skeptic
findings.refuted_by: the mirror running XOR also commutes with D1 and with the running XOR generates a lamp-free group (all 168 invertible 3 x 3 bit matrices at f = 3, 2,520 elements at f = 4, at least 3.08 million at f = 5); R8 with a Z-type halving gives a family whose limit is 0.79 to 0.85 away from the exact twin

findings.statement: At block 2, copy-by-copy exactification of any approximate unit costs at least 2W moves (plain) and separate scales at least 2(W + 1); so an approximate unit can save at block 2 only if it is kept and has between W + 1 and 2W - 1 moves, which needs closure to fail among kept programs.
findings.status_detail: it rests on Lemma W, which two skeptics upheld in an earlier round on approximate units; the skeptic of this track did not list this step among those it read line by line; no person has read it

findings.statement: Lemma Lambda1: a first-order approximate unit at block 2 needs at least 1.5W moves; a first-order 2 in 3 has exploding readouts of rank exactly 1 and base inputs of rank exactly 1.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic read it line by line and checked the smallest case exhaustively over the two-element field (4,032 solvable configurations, all with b = g = 1; none in the exact case)

findings.statement: Proposition Lambda-h: an approximate unit at block 2 with pole order h needs M >= W(h + 2)/(h + 1); an approximate W in W + 1 needs pole order at least W - 1.
findings.status_detail: proved when the coefficients are numbers or matrices; only argued in the limit algebra (where h = 1 is Lemma Lambda1); one skeptic checked the field case

findings.statement: Proposition Lambda2: the simplest first-order approximate 2 in 3 at block 2 is the same as an exact triangular 2 in 3 (outputs K x + T y and K y); without collapses such a program is impossible.
findings.status_detail: Lambda2 checked by hand by one skeptic; the 'needs collapses' step is argued only

findings.statement: The triangular search (36 penalised runs, six direction patterns, three menus) found only a trade-off curve residual x |T| of about 0.5 to 0.8, never a program with bounded cross-term T; unpenalised runs fell only because T grew.
findings.status_detail: a numerical search found nothing; this is evidence, not proof; the skeptic re-evaluated the runs on new inputs at f = 2, 4, 6 (products 0.47 to 0.65, and 0.82 to 0.89 at f = 6)

findings.statement: A 'border family' for 2 in 3 at block 2 whose error kept falling as its coefficients grew had been fitted to a single random input; on fresh inputs one array missed by 3.2 to 5.7 times the target.
findings.status_detail: refuted by a fresh-input test
findings.refuted_by: a fresh-input re-evaluation by the round's skeptic: one array misses by 3.2 to 5.7 times the target, and by 75 to 99 % with its readout refitted (the fit had 464 complex unknowns against 672 equations at f = 2 and 3, and one random input vector)

findings.statement: Search rules: W arrays need W independent routes into the target layer and, by transposition, W out of the inputs; a unit with exactly W + m - 1 moves is one chain; the division by 2 must come after a move and before a move in the reversed program; a transposed unit is a unit.
findings.status_detail: no skeptic read the rules as a whole; one skeptic re-derived one corollary of the top rule

findings.statement: Two arrays can be separated with two pieces using the order-3 cyclic shift sigma of three address bits: from x1 + x2 and x1 - sigma x2 the transform of x1 is recovered exactly, because 1 + sigma is invertible.
findings.status_detail: checked with matrices at blocks 3 and 4; upheld; used in the block-4 section

findings.statement: Against Theorem 2W' (a mixed unit needs at least 2(W_K + W_R) moves), the widened mixed units with hook room 32 that the wave-1 skeptic listed, 9+53 in 121, 10+57 in 131 and 5+32 in 72, would need 124, 134 and 74 moves and are excluded; widened 2+10 in 24 sits exactly on the bound; the engine units with room 16 to 48 (12+44 in 113, 11+40 in 103, 14+53 in 135, 13+49 in 125, 12+45 in 115, 11+41 in 105, 14+54 in 137) have one move to spare. Engine 12+44 in 113 and 14+53 in 135 are also exactly tight on Theorem M's certificate (2,260 of 2,260 and 2,700 of 2,700), so the symmetric track's term-by-term argument would exclude them.
findings.status_detail: the author's arithmetic for this write-up, on top of Theorem 2W' (one skeptic) and the symmetric track's term-by-term argument (no skeptic); no skeptic has checked it; the archive's catalogue still lists 9+53 in 121 as open

open.question: Is there a kept approximate 2 in 3 at block 2 in the everything-free game (or 3 in 4, 3 in 5), i.e. does closure fail among kept programs for W + 1 <= M <= 2W - 1?
open.first_experiment: Re-run tri_als.py with a menu containing braid-capable phases, parity phases, the mirror running XOR and Toffoli-type steps, penalising the cross-term; a hit is a run with fresh residual below 0.05 at f = 5 and cross-term under twice the signal. In parallel, prove Proposition Lambda-h in the limit algebra.

open.question: Block 3 with everything free: is there a 2 in 5 or 3 in 6 (exactly on max(W + 3, 2W)), or a 3 in 7 or 3 in 8 above it?
open.first_experiment: Readouts 1 - g with g a free word of large order (start with A.B), contents built from powers of g, orbit sums truncated at length L; run the exact cross-talk test as L grows. Proof side: finish the third-layer case split (W = 2, M = m + 2), which would close 2 in 5 here and 2 in 7 at block 5; 3 in 6 needs the same step for W = 3.

open.question: Conjecture FT: does touching a two-row array completely always cost at least 8 of the hook's room, for non-Levi steps, non-abelian groups and moves that touch several arrays at once, with a version for partly touched arrays?
open.worth: with the versions for partly touched arrays and for moves that touch several arrays, it would exclude every remaining room-16 block-3 mixed unit
open.first_experiment: Extend the abelian-Levi proof to the non-abelian letter group of order 8 already tested by fulltouch4.py; test letter groups of order 16 and more and three packed arrays; then state the partial version (removing a fraction x costs at least 8 g(x) with g(0.4) > 0.4).

open.question: Is there an engine (or widened) 1+5 in 12 at block 3?
open.first_experiment: Build candidates whose first touches use several steps (at least 5 on the kernel array), with input and readout directions of the one-move layer exact complements, and price them with the 105-dimensional certificate tools before any search.

open.question: Is there an engine 10+36 in 93 or a widened 2+9 in 22 at block 3?
open.first_experiment: Run the f = 2 screen (fam.py) on 10+36 in 93, never searched, with every kernel array first touched by at least 3 steps; for 2+9 in 22, a search built around the order-4 twist loophole.

open.question: Is the f = 2 floor 0.25 of kernel-relay shapes a theorem?
open.first_experiment: Prove exactly, from the 4-move relay 1+1 in 4, that a kernel array whose middle move is shared with a two-row array's top can never supply the characters 001 and 101.

open.question: Block-3 mixed units with more room (engine 12+44 in 113, 11+40 in 103, 14+53 in 135, 13+49 in 125, 12+45 in 115, 11+41 in 105, 14+54 in 137; widened 2+10 in 24): any of them?
open.first_experiment: Have a skeptic check the term-by-term argument on Theorem M's certificate, which on the author's own unchecked arithmetic already excludes engine 12+44 in 113 and 14+53 in 135 (both exactly tight there: 2,260 of 2,260 and 2,700 of 2,700); then apply the first-touch lemmas to the rest as was done for 10+36 in 93 (minimum number of steps in each kernel array's first touch), and screen the survivors at f = 2.
